assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin biology, proglucagon-derived peptides, receptor signaling) led to durable, widely used therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity with demonstrated cardiovascular and renal benefit; this is one of the largest translational impacts in recent medicine, and the mechanistic discovery is clear and original.
assessment.attribution: Drucker and Holst established GLP-1 physiology and its therapeutic rationale; Knudsen led development of long-acting, clinically effective analogues. Mojsov's structural and peptide-identification contribution is a real credit question that a three-person cap cannot fully resolve, and other early contributors may sit outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation across physiology, multiple independent drug programs and very large outcome trials; interpretation is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Fair division between basic physiology and drug development, and Mojsov's credit, is unresolved.
Long-term safety and population-level outcomes are still accumulating.
Whether recognition should favor discovery over industrial development is a committee judgment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstrating that TNF is a dominant driver of synovial inflammation and that its blockade controls rheumatoid arthritis transformed rheumatology and extended to inflammatory bowel disease, psoriasis and spondyloarthritis; the conceptual shift (a single cytokine as a tractable target in a chronic polygenic disease) is original and durable.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini are the established pair for the cytokine-hierarchy concept and the clinical proof of concept with anti-TNF antibody. Credit for TNF cloning and for antibody engineering involves other scientists who are not in the supplied names, so attribution to two people is defensible but not free of dispute.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty-five years of clinical use and independent replication; the field is mature and recognition is not premature. Flagged: as a rheumatologist I may weigh this field too heavily and have tried to apply common criteria.
uncertainties: Contributions of other TNF researchers and of antibody engineers could be viewed as decisive.
Prior prizes in adjacent biologics areas may affect the committee's appetite.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational inhibition of BCR-ABL turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable one and established the template for kinase-targeted oncology, including the demonstration of resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery), Druker (clinical proof of concept) and Sawyers (resistance biology and next-generation inhibitors) map to distinct decisive roles. Earlier discoveries of BCR-ABL and the Philadelphia chromosome are not credited here and would need to be treated as background.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with two decades of survival data and independent confirmation; timing is ripe and arguably long-standing.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should reflect the earlier oncogene discoveries instead of or in addition to the drug is a boundary question.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway defined how cytosolic DNA is sensed and triggers type I interferon and inflammatory responses, with implications for infection, cancer immunotherapy, autoinflammation and lupus-like autoimmunity; it is a conceptually clean and original innate-immunity discovery.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cyclic dinucleotide second messenger cGAMP; Barber identified STING. Other credited contributors (Ishikawa, Sun, Wu) played real roles, but the decisive pair is defensible. Others outside the supplied list, such as the cyclic-dinucleotide and bacterial CDN work, may complicate it.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across many laboratories and now in clinical development, though therapeutic payoff is still emerging, so some may argue it is slightly early.
uncertainties: Therapeutic modulators have not yet delivered approved drugs.
Overlap in STING discovery between groups and credit for parallel work is not fully settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened the field of genetically engineered cellular immunotherapy, and now also move toward autoimmune disease; clinical impact and conceptual novelty are high.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain led the design and clinical translation of CAR constructs with costimulation; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified T cells. Original CAR concept credit (Eshhar and others) is outside the supplied names, which is a concern for attribution.
assessment.maturity: Approved products and multi-year follow-up exist; solid-tumor results remain limited. Recognition is reasonable but the story is still evolving.
uncertainties: Original chimeric receptor concept credit lies outside the supplied credited names.
Toxicity, relapse and access limitations remain.
Immunotherapy was recognized in 2018 so overlap may be argued.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity and is a foundational experimental tool across neuroscience and physiology, with early clinical applications in vision restoration; its originality and breadth of influence are very high.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (with Bamberg) discovered and characterized channelrhodopsin; Deisseroth and Boyden demonstrated neuronal use; Miesenböck made an earlier genetically targeted light-control proposal. Six credited names cannot be reduced to three without leaving out a decisive contributor, so this is the most contested configuration.
assessment.maturity: Widely confirmed and used for two decades; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Three-person limit excludes Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck, each with a plausible claim.
Impact is mainly as a research tool rather than a therapy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical and other cancers, with population-level reductions in disease already documented; it is a landmark in preventive medicine and vaccine technology.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed the L1 VLP approach; Frazer led parallel VLP work and early vaccine development. Contributions from other groups (including Zhou, the late Jian Zhou) are outside the supplied names, so the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Strong real-world effectiveness data and independent confirmation; recognition is timely, though HPV's link to cancer was already recognized in 2008.
uncertainties: Prior Nobel recognition of the HPV-cancer link may be thought to cover this area.
Credit disputes among groups that developed VLPs.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of IL-6 and its receptor signaling and the therapeutic blockade of IL-6R led to treatments for rheumatoid arthritis, giant cell arteritis, cytokine release syndrome and other inflammatory conditions; the discovery is original and clinically significant.
assessment.attribution: Kishimoto and Hirano cloned and characterized IL-6 and defined its receptor biology; tocilizumab development was led from Kishimoto's setting. The pair is a coherent credit configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mature with long clinical use, but the therapeutic impact is somewhat narrower than TNF blockade and a prize in the cytokine area may be seen as overlapping with other anti-cytokine candidates. Field proximity noted as a possible bias.
uncertainties: Overlap with the TNF candidate may argue for choosing only one cytokine-blockade prize.
Other contributors to IL-6 discovery may be argued as decisive.
